system.name: Rowan-KV
system.one_liner: a persistent-memory key-value store that uses Rowan's one-sided RDMA abstraction for low-DLWA primary-backup replication

components.name: CM
components.role: configuration manager that maintains shard-to-server distribution, cached by servers and clients

components.name: per-shard hash indexes
components.role: DRAM-resident hash tables indexing objects in t-logs or the b-log for every shard the server manages

components.name: RDMA

content.key_idea: Rowan-KV shards and replicates key-value data across servers, using local per-thread logs for client writes and a single shared backup log per server (written one-sidedly over RDMA via Rowan) to minimize the number of PM write streams and thus write amplification.
content.reading_order: top-down/left-right: Clients issue requests through the CM-managed shard map to Server 1, which appends locally (t-logs), indexes in DRAM, and replicates over RDMA to the backup logs of Server 2 and Server 3.

summary: Rowan-KV is a persistent-memory key-value store built on the Rowan RDMA abstraction to achieve low-latency, low-write-amplification primary-backup replication. Figure 5 shows its architecture: clients send RPCs to the primary server of a shard (tracked by a configuration manager, CM); each server keeps per-thread logs (t-logs) in PM for local PUT/DEL appends, a single backup log (b-log) in PM that receives replication writes from primaries via one-sided Rowan, and DRAM-resident per-shard hash indexes. The figure depicts Server 1 as primary replicating to Server 2 and Server 3 as backups over RDMA, with circled step numbers marking the local log append, the replication write, and the index update. The diagram uses a light blue/green/gray flat palette with dashed server boundaries, colored GET (blue) and PUT/DEL (red) arrows, and a small table representing the CM's shard-to-server mapping at the top.
